videos.title: Water Polo Strength & Conditioning
videos.overview: Comprehensive dryland and in-water conditioning series covering active dynamic mobility, resistance-band rotator cuff prehab, core rotation, and in-water wrestling, positioning, and partner endurance drills.

videos.title: Water Polo 2m Position
videos.overview: Center forward (hole set) and 2-meter defender battles: ball-side positioning, hand-fighting, split eggbeater leverage, turning/sealing, drawing exclusions, defensive recovery.

videos.title: Water Polo Offense
videos.overview: Perimeter driving, releases, and defender manipulation: separation against a press, feeding the center, fast-twitch direction changes.

videos.title: Water Polo Defense
videos.overview: Perimeter press defense, tactical fouling, drop/crash positioning, driver denial. High hips, forearm leverage, perimeter awareness.

videos.title: Water Polo Passing and Shooting
videos.overview: Live passing, ball protection under pressure, beating splitters, shoulder fakes and hitches, finishing releases.

videos.title: Water Polo Fundamentals
videos.overview: Aquatic movement, eggbeater mechanics, elevation, horizontal-to-vertical balance, slide-and-shoot progressions.

videos.title: USAWP Base Position Fundamentals
videos.overview: The base position for faking, passing and shooting: tripod legs and left arm, chest forward, shoulders 30-45° off the goal, elbow at ear height behind the shoulder line, wrist facing the target; the mistakes that break it; internal rotation; and the drills that build it.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Eggbeater
videos.overview: The eggbeater as ODP teaches it: balanced start, wide base, high knees, flat feet.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Repeat Breaststroke Kicks
videos.overview: Short fast breaststroke kicks from a 45° chest angle as the only power source, then the reach lunge.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Spidering technique
videos.overview: Working efficiently in the horizontal position, hips above chest, ready to explode.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Skating + Lunging
videos.overview: Explosive 45° glides from the horizontal position, then the reach lunge that helps back to the center.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP Reverse Sculling
videos.overview: Moving backward on the hip with the legs doing the work: the base of the zone position, drive defense and inside water.

videos.title: Water Polo: ODP ball handling drills
videos.overview: Warm-up, station or variety work with the ball: balance, core, legs and hand-eye.

clips.title: Series Introduction & Training Philosophy
cues: Overview of the multi-module system: dryland mobility, functional strength, in-water body movement, perimeter play, center play, fitness.

clips.title: Active Dynamic Stretching Protocol
cues: Dynamic, continuous movement over static holding.
Full-body: shoulders, thoracic spine, groin, hip flexors, knees, wrists, ankles.

clips.title: Upper-Body Mobility: Arm Swings, Butterfly & Elbow Spins
cues: Forward/reverse arm circles (6–12 each); two-arm butterfly swings; elbow spins and wrist rotations (shot snap); single-arm rotational swings into throwing posture.

clips.title: Lower-Body Mobility: Hips, Groin & Hamstring Series
cues: Seated quad/hip pulls; butterfly stretch, partner-assisted hamstring; supine spinal twist; high-knee chest pulls replicating eggbeater chambering.

clips.title: Resistance Band Shoulder Prehab Routine
cues: 15 min before every water workout.
Scarecrow row; elbow-pinned internal/external rotations at steady cadence; standing fake-throw with core rotation; triceps snap-through.

clips.title: Dryland Before the Water: Push-Up Variations
cues: 10-15 minutes before every water session: push-ups, sit-ups, squats, pull-ups, planks.
Push-up: body flat, no bottom in the air, no sagging back.
Hand positions - wide, narrow (triceps), one high one low - ten of each; in the game your pushing hand is never in the same place.

clips.title: Core: Taco, Bicycle, Flutter, Scissor, Six Inches
cues: Taco: legs and upper body up together, pivot on the hip bone, don't push off the hand on the ground - stomach does the work; the hardest sit-up there is.
Bicycle: arms and legs as pistons, right to left.
Legs and arms up together pivoting on the lower back. 20-30 seconds each, move on.
Flutter kick, scissor kick, or hold six inches off the ground.

clips.title: Air Squats
cues: Exactly what an eggbeater looks like underwater: knees up into the groin, wide frame, great foundation.
No weight room - do many.
Knees never past the toes, lower back flat as if sitting into a chair, head up.
Deep squats past 90° only if you can.

clips.title: One-Legged Lunges
cues: Alternate, or ten in a row on one leg.
Reach as far as possible; front knee not past the toes; back knee within a half inch to an inch of the ground; back stiff and still, upper body vertical, no hunching over the stepping knee.

clips.title: The Genie
cues: Air squat plus explosion: deep squat to a vertical jump, snapping off the toes, as high as you can.

clips.title: Planks and Variations
cues: Hands or elbows (the thinkers); body straight, no arch, bottom neither up nor down.
Alternate one hand off the ground; opposite arm and leg; advanced: same arm, same leg.
Side planks with one leg and one arm elevated - shoulder strength without strain.
A stronger core prevents injuries in the limbs.

clips.title: Back Extensions; Build a Full Dryland
cues: Back injuries are common in the sport; extensions strengthen around the vertebrae.
Alternate arms and legs, then both.
Combine push-ups, squats, one-legged lunges and sit-ups into one whole-body block; 20-25 minutes on land before the water, some breaking a sweat.
It prevents injury and readies the body for the skills.

clips.title: Swim Conditioning: Fly-Free, Vertical Fly, Vertical Breast
cues: Fly-free: butterfly arms with a strong freestyle kick, upper body out of the water.
Vertical fly: two breaststroke kicks (one short and quick, one long and powerful) to one pull, ribcage out of the water.
Vertical breast: both arms push down toward the waist, elevate a half hitch higher; double kick, then kick out horizontal and glide.

clips.title: Head-Up Flutter Kick; Five Strokes to a 360
cues: Flutter kick head up, hands sculling out front, chest as high as possible, feet exiting the water and whitewater behind - the most unused drill in the game.
Five hard head-up strokes, horizontal to vertical, propel out of the water into a full 360; alternate left and right; surface with the head above water so the game is still in front of you.

clips.title: Suicides With Variations
cues: Basketball suicides in the pool, before games and practice: change of direction with a variation in the middle.

Reach-stroke lunge as if knocking someone down; head-up swim like a counter; field-block position - rotate over the hips, step with the leading hand into the water, lean on it and elevate, walk out four or five meters and finish with a big lunge.
Out of the water at each end for push-ups, sit-ups, air squats.
Five hard head-up freestyle into five lunges and back. 100% - the game is too fast for a slow-twitch player.

clips.title: Band Work: Swim, Eggbeater and Breaststroke Kick Through Resistance
cues: Torture for players, entertainment for coaches.

Swim out against the band for a minute, cycling freestyle kick, breaststroke kick and eggbeater: learn to swim through being held, grabbed or pushed under and keep the arms going so the referee sees it.
Eggbeater on the band: frame and leg strength; resistance grows the further you go, pushing past the threshold - goalies, 2 m defenders and centers most of all.
Breaststroke kick on the band too: as much of our game as the eggbeater.

clips.title: Band Work: Faking in the Tripod; Kick With the Ball; Dives
cues: Ball in hand on the band: fake from a shooting position, tripod with the leading hand sculling and the legs driving forward, 15-30 seconds; wears them down now, pays off in the fourth quarter.
Leading shoulder stays out of the water - the leading hand sculls it up.
Breaststroke kick with the ball against the band: moving into open pockets to make or re-make shooting lanes.
Dives on the band: vertical to horizontal, snap the legs under, chest out, big fake, drop and kick into the next pocket.

clips.title: Dive Forward, Step Back
cues: Dive into the open water in front of you with the leading hand, vertical to horizontal with a breaststroke kick; one forward, one back.
Underwater: straight vertical tripod to an elongated horizontal, then legs snapped back under to hold the vertical.
Ball stays dry - the moment it enters the water a defender can jump you.

clips.title: Fake Forward, Step Back (vs Zone or Split)
cues: Attack the defense; when the defender jumps out, keep the ball live and step back to absorb or anticipate the jump, then immediately re-attack.
Split eggbeater snaps hips back into a protecting position, knees back in to return to vertical; the tripod hand buys the half inch to pass over or around him.
Diving forward finds open pockets and new lanes - the defense can't move as fast as your kick.
After every dive get back past the ribcage and make the defense honor you before the next move.

clips.title: Walking Tripod With a Weighted Ball
cues: Ribcage out, leading hand sculling out front to protect you; leading leg directly under the left shoulder for balance; back (right) leg pushing forward, keeping you in the attack.
Bad clips: leaning too far forward, sculling hand not keeping the shoulder up, leading leg behind - faster, but no height.
Add a small rhythm fake to stay in control and balanced; lift the tripod hand out of the water to force the legs to hold you vertical.
Knees wide and high - the legs feed the wolf: strong legs give you vision over everyone.

clips.title: Heavy Ball: 40/20 and the Explosion Drill
cues: Heavy ball or weight belt to push the legs.
Knees high and wide, 40 seconds on, 20 off.
Advanced: a big breaststroke kick explosion out of the water every 5-10 seconds, 30/30 or 40/20, 10-12 rounds; both legs generate force and a big kick lifts the torso.

clips.title: Heavy Ball to Sprint
cues: Wrestle the ball up for 10-20 seconds, straight into a 25 or 50 head-up freestyle sprint - the game goes from wrestling to sprinting.
No heavy ball: partner up and wrestle into the sprint.
Breaststroke kick launches the swim; head up through the change of direction; kick hard - the arms are the boat and the wheel, the legs are the motor.

clips.title: Heavy Ball Shooting, Fatigued
cues: Heavy ball over the head 15-20 seconds, then throw it as hard as you can and receive six balls to shoot; or a leg set with the heavy ball, then dry receive horizontal to vertical to shoot, four to six shots.
Proper body position while tired: the fourth-quarter shot has to be as good as the first.
Buy one; use it every day in passing, shooting and legs.

clips.title: Wrestle-Swim and Grind-Out
cues: Wrestle 10-20 seconds for position, controlling elbows and arms, then an immediate 15, 25 or 50 m head-up sprint, back to wrestling.
Grind-out swim: cutting each other off, barreling down the pool - more aggressive than a game while staying clean.
Jump back on each other the moment you return; be a step ahead mentally.
Watch the underwater physicality and leg work.

clips.title: Push War
cues: Arms locked at the shoulders, facing each other, pushing with a horizontal eggbeater for 10-15 seconds; release, separate 4-5 m, and go straight into a defensive skill - KO lunge, field block, or a reach-freestyle sprint back.
Legs from pushing to defense without a break.

clips.title: In-Water Resistance: Arm Lock Drill
cues: Body contact while protecting the ball; torso at 45°; split eggbeater — lead leg straight down under shoulders, back leg at 45° driving forward.

clips.title: Conditioning & Wrestling: Dead Man Swimming Drill
cues: Groups of three; two wrestle 5–10 s, sprint to wall on whistle; winner rests, loser stays in against the fresh player.
Cut off pursuit angles, keep the opponent on your back/hip.

clips.title: Tactical Water Protection: The Human Shield Drill
cues: Protect an open ball without touching it; back to defender; continuous split eggbeater; elbows out in a straight line = "your water"; never swing elbows back past the midline.

clips.title: Center Trench Warfare Philosophy
cues: Games are won at center.
Winning ball side forces the defense into a drop, opening driving and outside shooting lanes.

clips.title: Ball Control Drill (BC Drill)
cues: Ball stays within the shoulder frame; hands slide under, never slap over; split eggbeater — one leg vertical, opposite leg at 45° behind.
Ball outside the frame = a steal.

clips.title: Defend Your Opponent Drill (DYO Drill)
cues: Control the jumping defender before going to the ball.
Breaststroke kick to seal the attacked side; near shoulder wedges, far hand controls the ball; head up for crashers and goalie.

clips.title: Face Turn & Seal Drill
cues: Ball on the weak-side triangle (1–2), center faces the strong side (4–5).
The moment the ball enters the strong side: under-armpit hook, rotate hips, seal before the pass arrives — or it is an offensive foul.

clips.title: Stroke & Spin vs. Stroke & Slip
cues: Fronted tight: fake a hard stroke, chin to chest, whitewater, spin 180° behind the defender.
Separation: skip the spin, slip the inside arm under the armpit and kick through. (Slip at `00:06:33`.)

clips.title: Squirm Drill (Wide Frame)
cues: The center learns to control and push back his defender: high out of the water, chest line showing, arms sculling to make a wide frame the 2 m defender can't jump around.
Elbows never go back past the body frame - that is an offensive foul; inside the frame that water is yours.
Work rate of arms and legs, whitewater everywhere.
Wider = easier to keep ball side.

clips.title: Relax, Then Squirm on the Entry
cues: Ball not coming in: the center relaxes.
The moment he knows it is coming he squirms into the defender and establishes dominance at set - and earns the exclusion.

clips.title: Squirm Swim Release (Two-Stroke to a Dunk)
cues: The squirm keeps the defender's hips up and creates small separation; the instant you feel it, release into a two-stroke swim for the dry pass and the slam dunk.
Never push off the defender and reach - show the referee you are swimming away before the ball comes.
Underwater: legs come up into you, big breaststroke kick starts the separation, two strokes, catch, finish.

clips.title: Squirm to a Quick Shot
cues: Squirm back into the defender, gain the position, release to the ball.
The defender is worried about getting hit or getting around as the ball is delivered - that is your separation.
If the shooting arm is free, shoot.
Don't wait for him to get back on you.
Quick twitch from squirm to shot beats any 2 m defender.

clips.title: Inside Water Shooting Drill
cues: Defender directly on your back, cage in front.
Squirm first; as the ball comes, a quick shoulder spin creates the distance from defender to ball.
Head buried in the chest but eyes on the cage.
Don't expect the call - go forward with the shot.
From above: the off shoulder and off elbow turn into the defense, the shooting arm is free, the off hand fends him off - a clean, high-percentage shot.

clips.title: Strong-Side Corner Turn, Cross-Cage Low
cues: Ball from the 5 or the 1: strong side and corner turn established before the ball arrives, separating to the strong side with the defender on your weak-side arm.
Leading hand high with the ball to make the goalie rise; best shot is cross-cage low under his arms.
The off shoulder shields the defender from your shooting arm.
Legs: split eggbeater, quick hip twist, foundation leg (right for a right-hander) directly under you, step out over it.

clips.title: Weak-Side Quarter Turn: 360 Spin, or Shield and Draw
cues: Right-hander set on the 1-2 side, squirming before the ball comes.
Quarter turn powered by the split eggbeater into a 360 spin; the arm stays above the head, not out over the defender, so he can't hit it.
Underwater: the near leg high and horizontal, knee or shin shielding him off - go straight vertical and he jumps on top of the arm.
Not every set shoots: with position, shield him off with the left arm and shoulder, take the ball right-handed to inside water, and take the 5 m or the exclusion.

clips.title: Center Offense Recap
cues: Head above water; work rate of legs and arms; split eggbeater - one leg under you as the foundation, the other pushing you back into the defender to hold the 2 m line.
Own the front court.

clips.title: 2m Defense: Control Ball Side for the Whole Clock
cues: A 2 m defender who controls the game forces the offense into low-percentage post-ups and drives.
The best center-backs hold ball side for the entire shot clock, or lose it for a split second and take it back with a sharp move.

clips.title: Forearm Field Blocking
cues: Right forearm on the set, hands elevated to show you aren't grabbing; legs at 45° in the water so you can elevate into a block or steal.
Game clip: it takes part of the cage away from the shooter and narrows the goalie's job - a higher center block rate.

clips.title: Stroke Release
cues: Ball swinging from one triangle to the other: the 2 m defender re-establishes position with one stroke; the leading hand, once positioned, shows and takes away the entry.
From above he is horizontal with hips away from the set so he can't be grabbed; underwater ~45° so the breaststroke kick keeps contact and control.

clips.title: Two-Stroke Release From the Wrong Side
cues: Caught on the wrong side with the ball at the 5: stay and you're in trouble.
Two-stroke release, swim around, re-establish ball side.

clips.title: Push Release to a Jump
cues: Push to make distance so the set can't control you; it also makes him react to the lever on his body.
As he reacts, the 2 m defender jumps around with a big breaststroke kick to establish ball side.
Outside-hand stroke to get around, then both hands up to show the referee - no pushing, no sinking.

clips.title: Slip Move to the Front; Push Release When the Hips Are Down
cues: Slip: from directly behind, a big breaststroke kick maneuvers into a front; it aggravates the set and forces the offensive push.
Push release: for defenders losing the battle or with hips down - make distance, elevate the hips to horizontal, then breaststroke-kick back onto him to regain ball side.
Vertical is the bad position for the 2 m defender; the push release gets him horizontal again where he can't be controlled.

clips.title: Armpit / Shoulder Control
cues: The first technique taught to center defenders.
Inside hand controls the set at the armpit; outside hand stays visible for the perimeter; lower back and legs at the surface so there is power to push him further out.
Moving the arm from one armpit to the other lets you push him and control ball side.
Show the referee: not on top of him, handling him underneath.

clips.title: Save Yourself With the Lap Pull
cues: Ball passed in from the 3 / point: the center-back dives inside with a strong lap pull, strokes over, and steals it.

clips.title: Forearm Control, Hands Off (Advanced)
cues: Relies on the legs.
Forearms on the set's back or shoulders, hands off him - the referee sees you aren't holding, and you don't get excluded.
Hips and hands from above: the leading hand is free to reach.

Crossing from side to side: a big explosive breaststroke kick to penetrate - fast twitch is what separates the defender who holds ball side from the one who gets excluded - then straight into a hard eggbeater to hold.
Push him to the vertical and you can move him outside, past the 2 m line.

clips.title: 2m Defender: Suit Grab Spin-Out & Forearm Control
cues: Release body contact first, then spin laterally to ball side.
Forearm contact on the set's back/shoulder, not wrist or waist — take the game out of the referee's hands.

clips.title: 2m Defender: Absorb & Lunge Drill
cues: Don't drop vertical when the set backs down.
Stay at 45°, absorb with high hips; when the set squares to shoot, explode off a breaststroke kick to contest.

clips.title: 2m Defender: Jump Inside Control Drill
cues: Beaten inside: never swim over the back (exclusion or 5 m).
Stay horizontal, breaststroke kick around the side, inside hand hooks the armpit, outside hand up clean to deflect.

clips.title: Perimeter Philosophy & Fast-Twitch Manipulation
cues: Make the defender commit weight and hips one way, exploit the counter-momentum.
Fast-twitch over slow swimming.

clips.title: Fast-Twitch Drive & Step-Back Release
cues: Sell 2–3 explosive strokes; as the defender commits and drops hips, step back over your hips into the vertical. 1–2 m of separation to feed set or shoot.

clips.title: Advanced Release (Ball-Side Hip Rotation)
cues: Two strokes to the ball carrier; rotate hips flat along the surface (don't drop them); shins and knees brace into the defender underwater; control the ball with the outside hand.

clips.title: Dig & Pop Drill
cues: High-cadence slip strokes sell the drive; defender drops vertical; jump back over your legs into a high eggbeater to catch and redirect or feed.

clips.title: Two-Stroke Release for Smaller Players
cues: Sweep the inside arm across the defender's chest; the forearm becomes a shield; split eggbeater absorbs contact and keeps the passing window open.

clips.title: Right-Back Drill
cues: One crossing stroke to show the referee the hold, pop the chest out and return the ball live without stalling the clock.

clips.title: Drive-Up Release & High Post
cues: Teammate drives down, you drive up into the vacant lane to balance the water; horizontal swim → protective vertical wall.
High-post: receive at 5 m, draw the foul, direct shot.

clips.title: Step-Over Release and Step-Back Attack
cues: Step over your hips, across your body, from horizontal to vertical, stepping away to make space: body at 45° in a pivot, releasing back over the back leg into the opposite 45°.
Then the next step: if the defense stays off in the zone after your release, come across your body and step back over your legs into the attack.
Your job is to make the defense play you; if they aren't honoring you, make them.
It's no good setting a triangle if you can't deliver a live entry to set.

clips.title: Stunt Move
cues: Shake-and-bake: fast-twitch head/torso fake with whitewater, cut back against the defender's momentum, trail hand clears the hip.
Also keeps your defender from helping.

clips.title: Elbow Control & Inside Stroke Mechanics
cues: Outside hand locks the defender's elbow/triceps, inside hand takes a full stroke.
Own the elbow, own the torso angle.
If he spins, step back over hips or cut across his back inside.

clips.title: Grind & Shin Release
cues: Inside stroke plus hip contact, then shins slide up the defender's torso and push off cleanly.
Never kick with the bottom of the foot (contra-foul).

clips.title: Perimeter Defensive Principles
cues: Two breakdowns: losing ball-vs-man awareness, and dropping hips vertical (drivers spin or push off).

clips.title: Standard Absorbed Shoulder Control
cues: Lead hand/forearm on the attacker's lead shoulder while he holds the ball; body at 45° via breaststroke kick; the instant he releases, both hands up clean.

clips.title: The Slip Move Steal
cues: Attacker relaxes: breaststroke kick inside, knock the ball off the hand/elbow with the lead arm, raise the controlling arm to show no foul.

clips.title: Foul & Deny Drill
cues: Lunge, hit the elbow, tactical foul; rotate hips straight back into a 45° denial (split eggbeater); near hand takes the lane to set, trail arm sculls for height against the lob.

clips.title: Foul-to-Foul Drill
cues: Against the right-back: don't sit in denial; rotate over hips, second breaststroke kick, knock him down and foul again before a live entry.

clips.title: Foul & Crash Drill
cues: Their set has position: foul your man, spin over your hips, swim straight into the 2 m crash lane to double.

clips.title: Foul, Lunge, KO
cues: Shoulder control at 45°, looking behind you to see if set needs the foul and help.
Foul, then the lunge-KO: a breaststroke kick with the arms in shot-blocking position and the intent to knock him down - never give the shooter his shot.
Rotate over the hips, hips and chest near the surface as the spring for the kick.
Same movement for the 5, front court, splitting and zones; underwater, the hips get back under to kick out.

clips.title: Absorb the Push-Off, Lunge Back Out
cues: X5 absorbs the offensive player's push-off with hips up, then lunges back out to foul and protect the 2 m defender - impossible from the vertical, only from the horizontal.
X4 KO lunge for pressure;
X3 splitting to the 4 as he moves into his area.
Powerful and explosive.

clips.title: Head-In, Feet-Out Lunge (Zone)
cues: Head toward the center of the pool or 2 m, legs facing where you want to go, so you step over your legs to gain ground.
Swimming out to the guy is slower and less pressure; the lunge up and over the hips with the breaststroke kick gets you there quicker.
The hand in the water leads and steps out front; the upper body goes to the legs, the legs never drop under.

clips.title: Put Him Down: Hit the Arm, Blocking Hand Up
cues: Never put the player down with the shot-blocking hand - drop it and he shoots over you.
Blocking hand stays up and takes your side of the cage; the leading hand (the one working underwater) hits the throwing arm at the elbow, not the body - big players absorb a body hit and still shoot.
One big lunge, head in, feet out.
X3 example: one hand knocks the ball down, the other blocks.

clips.title: Crossover Steal (Vertical)
cues: Late in the game when you need the ball.

He is vertical, controlling the ball: fake both hands up, then the inside hand goes across his lower or mid back and pulls him into you while the outside hand crosses his body with a big breaststroke kick to the ball.
Pressure on the shoulder makes him drop and dig for a foul; as he goes under, both hands up, reach up and around, and take it.

clips.title: Crossover Steal (Horizontal, on the Release)
cues: He is releasing for the ball in a horizontal swim or a two-stroke release: sit back, anticipate the pass.
His hips are right in front of you - the inside hand strokes over the hips and reaches for the ball.
It looks like a normal swim stroke, not a pull or drag.
Disguised, and it works in games.

clips.title: Perimeter Defense: Hips Up, Kick, Don't Get Grabbed
cues: Control your man and play the chess game: hips up, body protected from the grab, moving in and out by rotating over the hips.
Breaststroke kick over eggbeater - more powerful, more explosive, quicker to knock somebody down.

clips.title: Forearm Absorb (Driver Defense)
cues: Horizontal, almost a stepping position.
Forearm on his shoulder, hand off the player - show the referee contact without holding.
Let him push you back; you are in control.
Body stays horizontal so when he rears back or receives, the legs are set to breaststroke-kick back on top of him to foul or control.

clips.title: Dropped Hips (Bad Example)
cues: Defender drops his hips vertical: the driver goes left, right or steps away and creates distance, and the defender has to get back horizontal before he can gain ground - a two-step process against a one-step one.
Keep the hips up.

clips.title: Sculling Driver Defense: Don't Take a Stroke
cues: Scull or step to keep the distance while keeping contact; eyes on the ball, hand on your man.
The driver takes five to eight strokes; if you can contain him sculling without taking a stroke you are a step ahead and can jump out.
Take strokes and you commit one direction - he pulls back on his legs, receives, and you are gone.
Legs and hands, never a swim.

clips.title: Protect Spin
cues: He grabs a limb and rotates for inside water: spin out of it and the referee sees you are not the one holding.
Perimeter defenders get excluded for facing him instead of spinning.
Hip to hip, never onto the back (that gives him leverage); horizontal, hips at 45°, elbow in contact, both hands out of the water.
Legs working keeps the hands free; if the legs stop you have nothing but hands, and that gets called.

clips.title: Facing the Hold (Bad Example)
cues: Struggling through the hold facing the defender with hands down looks like you are holding, and defense is always the one called. "He grabbed me" is not a defense - spin out of it.

clips.title: Extra Stroke Drill (Driver Defense at 2 Meters)
cues: Driver stops at the 2 m line: don't rest on his outside shoulder and reach over (5 m or exclusion).
The line is another defender — two extra strokes around, hips along the surface, take inside water.

clips.title: Inside 4-Meter Pressing Drill
cues: Unbroken contact with forearms, elbows or chest; head swivels man–ball; contact lost → find the man first, then the ball.
Hips up, never vertical.

clips.title: Passing Mastery & Setting the Defense
cues: Great passers freeze defenders until the last moment.
Horizontal → 45° keeps passing angles live; if the defender doesn't value you, you are wasting the open man.

clips.title: Step-Away Passing (Weak Side)
cues: Defender lunges to your strong side: step away.
Ball over the head, or a 360° eggbeater spin releasing without hesitation.

clips.title: Step to Strong Side (Cross-Face Reception)
cues: Cross-face catch exposes the blind side.
Step across into a split eggbeater diving to the strong side; off-hand digs laterally; breaststroke kick up and over the defender's hands.

clips.title: Step to Weak Side vs. Blindsiding Splitter
cues: Vertical → horizontal dive to the weak side; breaststroke kick clears the trailing arm; off-hand shields for half a second.

clips.title: Step-Back Pass to Set
cues: Against a zone knock-down: drop onto your back only momentarily (the 2 m defender can step out and steal), then snap hips and legs under and launch vertical to pass or shoot.

clips.title: Step-In Pass & Shoulder Hitching
cues: Attack the cage with the arm high so the splitter must commit; hitch the shoulders to make the goalie jump; slip the wrist pass to the open shooter.

clips.title: Hitch Wrist Pass to the Strong Side
cues: Big shoulder hitch, picture the goalie jumping, then at the last second a wrist pass back to the strong side (a lefty at 4-5, or an open right-hander).
Do it slow or methodical and nobody buys it - aggressive, so the arm is strong and the pass leaves right before the release.

clips.title: Receive-and-Fake
cues: Ball arrives cross-face or strong side; shoulder hitch or quick twitch the instant it hits your hand so the goalie sets on you.
Then pass to the open man, or get the goalie digging on his hands and pick a high corner.
Be in attack position on arrival, every time.

clips.title: Fake-Twist Pass
cues: Set up the cross-face pass by attacking the cage to shoot; get the goalie's hands out of the water, then follow through the motion with a pass to the weak side for a catch-and-shoot.
The 5 attacks strong and at the last second twists the core hard without telegraphing; on extra man the same fake-twist to the 4.

clips.title: Overhead Pass Disguised in the Fake
cues: Get blocker, goalie and defense focused on you, then a pass that crosses over your body without turning the shoulders: body faces the cage, the motion goes up, over and across the face.
The goalie never sees the next pass coming.

clips.title: Fake-Out Pass
cues: Attack with a wide fake and the ball comes straight out of the fake to the pass, no hesitation.
Highly disguised, easy to learn, throws goalies off balance.
Bonus: dive strong side at the same time so goalie and defense dive with you.
Offense is chess - whatever your body shows, go the other way at the last second.

clips.title: Great Passers Look Like Shooters
cues: What separates a great passer: the defense believes you are the finisher, and the pass comes at the last moment without hesitation or disguise.
Become the finisher and you become the playmaker.

clips.title: Zone Passing: Step Around the Defender to Set
cues: Practice every day.

Cat-and-mouse: change your lean, step left and come up to pass, step weak side up and around the defender, crossover with the inside hand for a new lane; step strong side is easier - legs set, leading hand already leading, powerful kick.
Pass around the defense, never through it.

clips.title: Lean and Over-the-Head Pass to Set
cues: Lean strong side, then bring the ball beyond the lean over your head - outside the defender's reach.
Underwater: body at 45° for a big breaststroke kick to penetrate; leading hand out front as the foundation to fall back on.

clips.title: Wrist Pass Back to Set
cues: The 5 with body facing the wrong way sees the center inside and wrists it back to set: a man advantage or a 5 m.
Crafty wrist, nothing telegraphed.

clips.title: Vertical Overhead and Cat-and-Mouse Wrap Pass to Set
cues: Attack hard to make the defender drop his hands, come low on the fake, then fast-twitch it over his head straight to set - the center has all the time he needs to earn the exclusion or 5 m.
The wrap: make him lean strong side for the over-the-head, then come back down under his elbow and armpit.
Same moves as the wrap and overhead shots.

clips.title: Step Weak Side Before You Receive
cues: Move one to two yards before the ball arrives: shot or pass to set from a new angle.
The defender watching the center can't move with you.
Underwater: horizontal while stepping, quicker in the water.
Variation: strokes across the body to re-establish the lane, more momentum and speed.

clips.title: Dive Strong Side Before You Receive
cues: The lefty dives strong side before the ball comes, creating the pass or shot lane; both hands and a big breaststroke kick power him past the defense.
Advanced: the defender catches up, so one more step and a lean strong side on top of the dive to pass around him.

clips.title: Zone Passing Summary
cues: Fast twitch to out-maneuver the defender; the chess game - show one thing, wrap back or over the head; move before you receive.
Make them focus on you so another player opens.

clips.title: Shooting: Think Like the Goalie
cues: Body position, leg position, wrist action, release point.
The goalie thinks like a shooter; if you only think like a shooter he is a step ahead.
Watch the players move to new shooting lanes with dives, the breaststroke kick and the leading hand - the thing that takes a player up a level.

clips.title: SDL Drill: Swim, Dive, Legs
cues: Out of a hard counter or filling a pocket: momentum forward, big breaststroke kick, leading hand out front steering; look around for your open man; then to your legs to pass or shoot.
Stay horizontal through the dive and only go vertical after you are in the pocket; hips drive up into the body, ribcage out of the water.

clips.title: Walk With the Ball
cues: Physical drill: keep control of the ball and the defender, stay vertical on your legs, get the shot off without a foul - the referee does not bail you out.
Non-throwing hand is a bent shield, never a stiff arm.
Add finishes: quick twitch lean strong side and shoot over the head; or the wrap around the armpit.

clips.title: Wrap Shot and Near-Side Power Shot
cues: Wrap: lean ball side, breaststroke kick through past the defender's armpit; the goalie reads cross-cage and you wrap it back near side.
Near-side power: the arm comes up and over the head, over and around the blocking hand - reach around the defense, never through it.
When the goalie isn't there and the blocker isn't paying attention, snap it strong side.

clips.title: Dive Strong Side, Wrist Cross-Cage
cues: Dive strong side and shoot hard strong side over the head.
Then the follow-up: the goalie follows your body to his strong side and at the last second you wrist it back cross-cage.
Keep the arm over your head, not wide over your body - wide lets goalie and blocker read it.
Identical motion until the last half second of wrist; disguise the lean.

clips.title: Step Weak Side Shooting
cues: Move before every shot; the more you move, the more space.
Step across the body with the leading hand and a big breaststroke kick around the defender - underwater the hand comes out and back in to lead.
Your defender is eggbeatering; your breaststroke kick is further, more powerful and quicker.
Eggbeater is for the foundation, not for quickness.

clips.title: Wrap Shot Under the Blocker's Armpit
cues: Goalies rely on the field blocker for part of the cage; beat the blocker near side and you score at every level.
Come vertical and high with the arm motion, then wrap back under his armpit - slow it down and you see the opening.
Works on 6-on-5 and in front-court offense.
Twist: legs as high as you can, ball kept low - the blocker thinks high and you sweep under his arm.
Examples from the 6 spot: fake, fake, stay vertical, wrap around the blocker.

clips.title: Overhead Shot
cues: The shot not many have the confidence to take.
See the window over the blocker's cap or ear before you receive - the shot is open on delivery.
Lean strong side and the blocker feels it; keep the shoulders still and take the arm from over your head to over the defender's head and nobody reads it.

clips.title: Lean Overhead From the 1 and 6 Spots
cues: Lean overhead creates the lane around the blocker; the 1 leans past the X1 defender; the 6 with a quick lean for an easy goal.
Know where the blocking arm will be before you receive, so the shot is in your mind before the ball is.

clips.title: Redirect Shot
cues: All levels; master it and you score more.
The receiving hand never comes back - it pushes the ball forward, redirecting it; the ball is barely in your hand and it beats the goalie before he can react.
With defense on, it catches them locked up.
Awareness of cage and goalie; pull the trigger before he expects it; it doesn't have to be hard, just quick.

clips.title: Shooting Mechanics: Fast-Twitch Shoulder Fakes
cues: Twitch the lead shoulder and release immediately.
Ball stays behind or above the head; bringing it forward costs the re-cock and lets goalie and blocker reset.

clips.title: Cross-Face Near-Side Shot
cues: Shoulders pre-aligned to the cage, not the passer; catch and release with zero hesitation before the goalie slides.

clips.title: Cross-Face Draw Shot
cues: Body horizontal, legs moving with the ball; step across to open a new lane, draw goalie and blocker near-side, snap the wrist cross-cage.

clips.title: Shooting Summary: Release Angles & Variety
cues: Quickness and deceptive release beat velocity.
Wrap, overhead, wrist cross-cage, fast-twitch near side.

clips.title: Foundations of In-Water Agility
cues: Seamless horizontal ↔ vertical transition is the foundation of every advanced skill.

clips.title: Treading Water & Eggbeater Mechanics
cues: Knees wide, thighs perpendicular to the surface at 90°; feet in independent circles, snapping; upper body still.
Error: piston/scissor kick → bobbing, no visual stability.

clips.title: Tabletop / Spider Drill
cues: Back flat on the surface; all four limbs sculling; legs = balance, arms = steering; quick 90° pivots.

clips.title: Slip Stroke Technique
cues: High-cadence freestyle recovery with high elbows, hands slice without pulling; legs coiled horizontal ready to kick away.

clips.title: Stepping Drill
cues: Body in a straight line at the surface; lead hand sculls, trail hand pulls to the hip.
Perimeter defenders sliding lanes; shooters stepping into pockets.

clips.title: Absorb & Drag Drill
cues: Defender stays horizontal while driven backward; forearm on chest/shoulder with open hands visible; hips at the surface ready to kick out when the attacker goes to pass or shoot.

clips.title: Left & Right Hip Swings (180° Switches)
cues: Lead foot breaks the surface as the legs tuck tight under the torso; instant 180° redirection without dropping vertical.

clips.title: Pendulum Swings (Front to Back)
cues: Same rule as the hip swings: bring the knees up into the midsection and the front-to-back transition is quick.
Bad example underwater: dragging the legs vertical from front to back - slow, and the player said so.

clips.title: Change-of-Direction Drills
cues: Knees up into the body with a hard breaststroke kick to go the opposite way; 5 m each way is enough.
The arm swing gets the momentum going and the leading hand out front turns the body toward the new direction.

clips.title: Stop-and-Go
cues: The sport is stop and go.
Stop on a dime with legs and arms; the breaststroke kick is what restarts you.
Stay horizontal, never fully vertical, so the next move is ready.
Aggressive arm speed sells the drive.

clips.title: Forward Lunge
cues: Note how high the player gets: he is lunging at the shooter and taking away part of the cage at once.
Advanced: one hand replaces the other without pause, so there is always a hand up and never a clear lane.

clips.title: Side Lunges (Splits)
cues: Front-court defense: lunge to stun or knock down a driver.
The opposite side of the body pushes you - right leg and right arm drive a dive to the left.
Underwater: legs curl up, then a massive breaststroke kick for the highest reach.

clips.title: Sitting-in-a-Chair Sculling Drill
cues: Core, lower back and shoulders.
Sit back in the chair with knees and toes above the water, arms sculling in circles to push forward.
The more you sit up with knees and toes in the air, the better it works.

clips.title: Dribbling: Head Up and Head Down
cues: Arms never touch the ball; they are only a safety guard to push it back in front.
The ball rides the bow wave in front of your head.
Do it at 100% - cruise at 60-70% and you lose the ball at game speed.

clips.title: Change Left and Right With the Ball
cues: Hand under the ball, never on top; move it across underneath with the breaststroke kick and the opposite hand pulling the torso the new way; a strong kick on every direction change.
Advanced players: grip the ball and do the same.

clips.title: Off-Hand Pick-Up
cues: Four or five hard strokes, off hand (left) to strong hand, and elevate horizontal to vertical.
No hand on top of the ball, no need for big hands.
Never pass hand to hand in the air; a shovel with both hands touching for a split second is allowed.

clips.title: Swim to Vertical
cues: Carry the ball on the counter or up the front court straight into a vertical pass.
Whitewater from arms and legs; the lead leg (left for a right-hander) drives up under the left shoulder - the foundation for height.
Watch the ribcage come out of the water.

clips.title: Vertical to Swim
cues: From a faking or passing position into a swim.
The breaststroke kick generates the direction; legs come up into you for maximum kick strength.
Do the drill at 100% and it transfers to the game.

clips.title: Reach-Free Pop (Backspin)
cues: European drill: reach, stroke, pop the ball with backspin so it returns to the other hand.
Ball control and position control at once; the stroking arm and the breaststroke kick work simultaneously.

clips.title: Reach-Free Pass to Yourself
cues: Same as the pop but passing to yourself.
Take a real freestyle stroke and pull water with the breaststroke kick; catch out front and keep the ball alive.

clips.title: Back-of-Hand Pass to Yourself
cues: Same drill, pass to yourself off the back of the hand: knuckles down to make a cup.
Energy still comes from the legs and the breaststroke kick.

clips.title: Reach-Back Pass
cues: Backstroke with the eggbeater; one arm stroke with the legs working at the same time, passing the ball hand to hand.
Keep it low and short - throw it high and you lose body control.

clips.title: Triple Threat / Tripod Position
cues: Ball up, ready to pass or shoot at any moment; rotate 360 to see every angle.
Lead hand far out front sculling; one leg directly under you, the other slightly up and pushing forward - that is the shot's power.
All three limbs separated for balance.
Air pocket between armpit and water = max height.
Elbow above the ear; below it strains the shoulder.

clips.title: Dive Moves: Creating New Passing Lanes
cues: Vertical to horizontal and back, in every direction: strong side, across the body, forward, backward.
Practiced every day at the university level.
The off hand leads and initiates the foundation; without it you fall flat and never surface vertical.

clips.title: Dive, Dive, Throw It Down
cues: 25 yd: dive, snap the legs back under into the vertical, dive again, then throw the ball down hard as if shooting.
Knees come up into the midsection on every recovery; the throw-down works lower back and stomach.

clips.title: Elbow Control on the Perimeter
cues: Face to face, never back to back (no vision of the cage).
Elbow control gives you control of the defender for a give-and-go or to receive.
Underwater: both bodies at 45°, pushing into each other - drop the hips and you lose the space.
Ball held the furthest possible distance from the defender.
Forearm into the chest is legal while the elbow stays underwater.

clips.title: Stiff Arm = Offensive Foul (Bad Example)
cues: Extended arm pushing on top of the defender's shoulder is a foul every time - keep the arm bent.
Back to the defense loses vision, loses ground when you turn to look, and gives the defender equal reach for 50-50 balls.
Every drill keeps moving; standing vertical is never a drill.

clips.title: Soft-Hands Drill
cues: Both hands out as paddles, passing among the group; vary who and which hand.
Works fast hands, reaction, awareness, and the thing nobody trains: being ready to receive right after you pass.

clips.title: Wrist Pass
cues: Arm as straight as possible and still; over-emphasize the wrist snap.
Elevate past the ribcage before every pass.
Quality over quantity - the wrist is the last control on the ball.

clips.title: Crunch Drill
cues: A pitcher falls forward off the mound; we have no mound, so the stomach throws the ball.
Above water the arm barely moves - the body throws.
Energy through the stomach, the arm, the wrist.

clips.title: Cross-Face Passing
cues: One of the hardest skills in the game.
Body faces the player you are passing to, not the one you receive from; fewer steps beats more steps.
Catch above the forehead, bring it back and release in one fluid motion.
Elevate as you receive, ready to pass.

clips.title: Pass at Your Max Height
cues: Every passing drill: get out of the water as high as possible.
Pass with shoulders in the water and chin on the surface in practice and that is what you do in the game; body out of the water lets the torso turn fast without resistance.

clips.title: Vertical-Horizontal-Vertical Drill
cues: Receive vertical, swim with the ball, back to vertical to pass - like the game.
The breaststroke kick starts the swim; the lead leg drives up into the chest to bring you back vertical.

clips.title: Scoop Pass and the Dive Into Open Water
cues: Scoop pass while swimming, on the counter or in the front court, with the outside hand.
The dive: a strong breaststroke kick with the leading hand steering into the open pocket, with or without the ball; receive, dive to open water, elevate, pass.
Fundamental passing is body positioning - the split eggbeater makes the pass.

clips.title: Leg Up / Step Up Shooting
cues: Shooter goes to the highest peak: hands and legs work together, torso out of the water; the higher you get, the harder and quicker the body rotates.
Underwater: a hard breaststroke kick almost in a split eggbeater, one leg behind, one directly under the leading (left) shoulder.
Long strong kick drives legs → torso → shoulder → elbow → wrist; ball off the middle finger with backspin for the snap.

clips.title: Pass, Slide, Catch and Shoot: Keep Moving
cues: Stay still and the field blockers hold or block you.
Pass, then slide to a new shooting lane reading the cage; catch and shoot near side or cross-cage.
Slide by diving to the strong side around the defender, snap the legs back under, then catch - or crossover with the leading hand.

clips.title: Pass, Slide, Catch & Shoot (H2 Dive Progression)
cues: Horizontal dive for 1–2 m into the lane, snap the foundation leg under to pop vertical, catch at peak height, finish.
Foundation leg = height, back leg = power.

clips.title: H2 Dive Counter-Attack Finishing
cues: Strokes with the ball, snap the lead leg under, quick dive to freeze the trailer, read the goalie, finish.

clips.title: Weak-Side Slide, Catch & Shoot
cues: Dive into the weak-side window before the ball arrives, shooting hand up during the slide, one-touch finish.
Shooters create their own movement.

clips.title: Why Fundamentals Win: Schroeder & Brooks
cues: Balance is the most important thing in athletics.
At Partizan the best coach worked only with the 10-and-unders, on balance in the water.
The pros shoot hard because they shoot accurately, and they shoot accurately because the base is sound.
Without fundamentals the game peaks.

clips.title: Base Position: The Tripod
cues: Start here every time you have the ball, whether faking, passing or shooting.
Left arm out to the left, left leg straight down, right leg slightly out to the right: a tripod.
Chest angled down, leaning forward.
Shoulders rotated 30-45° off the goal, never parallel.
Throwing shoulder pinched, elbow at ear height, wrist bent back and facing the goal.

clips.title: Common Base-Position Mistakes
cues: Over-rotating with the left shoulder pointed at the goal: inconsistent release point, slower release, more time for the goalie.
Legs too far under the shooting arm: you move laterally and cannot use the body for power or vary the release.
Lying on your back: easier, but no core in the finish, so you overshoot.

clips.title: Legs: Lift and Rudder; Lean Forward
cues: Open the legs as wide as possible.
The left leg carries the up-and-down load; the right leg is the rudder for lateral movement.
Chest faces the bottom so leg acceleration transfers forward into the shot.
Leaning forward is off balance by design; the left hand sculls to keep you from falling.
Start parallel to the goal and rotate the shoulders 30-45°.

clips.title: Elbow Behind the Shoulder Line
cues: Elbow at ear height, shoulder pinched, elbow always behind the line between the two shoulders.
This needs shoulder flexibility; over-rotating the body to fake it is the common error.
The wrist faces the goal wherever the arm is, so the full wrist motion is available at the end.

clips.title: The Wrist: The Finish
cues: The wrist faces the target at all times, from 90° back to all the way forward, and pushes through with all five fingers at once.
It sets accuracy and consistency.

clips.title: Common Wrist Mistakes
cues: Turning the wrist over on its side instead of facing the goal adds rotation into the motion and breaks consistency.

clips.title: Throwing Form at Full Speed
cues: Check the start: wrist forward, elbow at the ear, left hand slightly in front, shoulder pinched, chest forward.
The base does not change until the throw starts.
Sequence: hard breaststroke kick, internal rotation of the shoulder, wrist snap and follow-through.

clips.title: Base-Position Drills: Walks and Markers
cues: Walk 25 m and back holding the ball in base position; the position must not change, and the temptation is to over-rotate because it moves faster.
Same walk, eggbeater up and accelerate with the legs at every marker; the upper body must not move, so the legs learn to work apart from the torso.
Eggbeater down the pool at about 80%, then one hard breaststroke kick to full release height.

clips.title: Internal Rotation: Steal Time from the Goalie
cues: Internal rotation of the shoulder accelerates the release and adds power.
Timing is the game: accelerating at one point in the motion beats the goalie's reaction.
Isolate it before you combine it.

clips.title: Internal Rotation Drill
cues: Parallel to your partner, elbow at shoulder height, ball back, wrist bent.
Follow the internal rotation forward slowly until the ball touches the water in front of you; three or four reps, then pass with the same motion and full wrist extension.
Check: at the end, the elbow is not in front of the shoulder line.

clips.title: Wrist Drills: Deck Release and Hand-to-Hand
cues: On deck, shoulders parallel to the wall, release the ball over and over; the wrist faces the wall, bends all the way back and forward, and the release point off the fingers is the same every time.
In the water, walk down the pool eggbeatering and pass hand to hand with the wrists only; speed is irrelevant, full range and wrists facing each other are the point.

clips.title: Closing: Repetition Until It Is Natural
cues: Watching it and trying it twice changes nothing.
Repeat until the motion is automatic.
Body position in the water is the one fundamental that separates the best from the mediocre.

clips.title: ODP Eggbeater: Sitting in the Chair
cues: The most fundamental movement and the base for everything else.
Start balanced: Jesse Smith looks like he is sitting in a chair.
Wide base, wide hips, hip flexibility, knees high, feet flat.
The common youth error is pointed toes, which make no force.
Eggbeater, short breaststroke kicks, and the transition between them are the foundation of all movement in the water.

clips.title: Short Fast Breaststroke Kicks at 45°
cues: Chest at 45°, facing forward, hands out of the water, short fast breaststroke kicks as the only power source.
Laps of 25 m or yd with a break between, repeated.
Foundation for movement in the water and for a strong eggbeater.

clips.title: Add the Reach Lunge; Vary the Angle
cues: Once the 45° kick is strong, add a reach lunge to simulate the steal, knocking a player down, and explosive defensive position.
Game use: pressing without fouling, pressure on the ball, defense with the legs.
As athletes develop, run the same kicks from horizontal and vertical positions.
Every youth practice, every week.

clips.title: Spidering: Horizontal, Hips Above Chest
cues: On the stomach, body compact, all four limbs fast: hands scull and pull, legs eggbeater.
Chest down and hips higher than the chest so the body can spring into an explosive movement at any time.
Uses: helping on a ball-side drive, helping at center, lunging into a lane for the steal, horizontal defense on the wings at the bottom line.

clips.title: Spider to Reach Lunge
cues: From the spider, a breaststroke kick into a lunge: pull with the hands, breaststroke kick with the legs, reach with the arm for the steal.
Three limbs together.
Repeat weekly.

clips.title: Skating: Explosive 45° Glides
cues: Horizontal, stomach to the bottom, hips above chest.
Reach out and glide at 45° angles, from the eggbeater into an explosive breaststroke kick, two kicks per side, and see how much ground you cover.
Kick, pull and reach at the same time.
Watch your hands as a goalkeeper watches the block.
Game use: recovering in the zone, helping on defense, helping back on the center.

clips.title: Skate + Reach Lunge
cues: After the 45° skate, the lead hand pulls water, the legs breaststroke-kick, and the opposite arm reach-lunges as far as possible: helping back to steal the ball from the center.
Dynamic horizontal defense.

clips.title: Reverse Sculling ("Bicycling")
cues: On the side or hip, not the chest, body in a straight line in the direction of travel, moving backward.
Legs high: lead leg at the surface, bottom leg no more than two feet down, pedaling at a high rate; the legs do the vast majority of the work.
Bottom arm pushes water, top arm pulls.
Learn it on both hips.
Basis for the zone defensive base position, drive defense and attacking inside water.

clips.title: Dry-Ball Freestyle and Backstroke
cues: Freestyle with the ball in front of the face on a steady short breaststroke kick.
Backstroke with the ball above the head; variant with the ball dry in front in a water polo backstroke motion.
Balance, core strength, leg strength, hand-eye coordination.

clips.title: Ball in Hand
cues: Advance with the ball gripped in the hand, as if a defender were beside you.
Not everyone can grip it; strive for it.
Short breaststroke kicks throughout.
Stop into a vertical position as in transition or counterattack, then back to ball in hand.

clips.title: Elbow Swim
cues: Advance with the hand under the ball, not on top of it, on a short breaststroke kick.

clips.title: Hand Transfer in Transition
cues: Three or four head-up strokes with the ball, transfer from the weak hand to the strong hand above water, and immediately go vertical into a double-threat position: the counterattack with a defender closing.

clips.title: Pressure Passing
cues: Ball behind the head, breaststroke away from the defender to protect it, then up vertical to pass or shoot away from him.
Ball above the head at all times, short breaststroke kicks, never bring it in front of the face.

groups.title: Fundamentals — legs and body position
groups.description: Everything else sits on this. If your eggbeater bobs or your hips drop, no drive, release or shot works. Watch the bad eggbeater in the first clip once, then don't be that guy.

groups.title: Perimeter offense — releases and drives
groups.description: How we get open on the perimeter. Fast-twitch sells the drive; the step-back over your hips is what actually creates the pass. Start with the drive/step-back and dig-and-pop; the hip-rotation release and grind/shin are varsity.

groups.title: Perimeter defense — press, foul, deny
groups.description: Two ways we break down: losing ball-and-man, and dropping our hips. Hand on the shoulder while he has the ball, hands up the instant he passes. Foul-and-deny is our default when set has position.

groups.title: 2 m offense — ball control and sealing
groups.description: Ball stays inside the shoulders, hands under it. Control the defender before the ball. Face-turn and seal the moment the ball crosses into the strong side.

groups.title: 2 m defense — absorb, lunge, recover
groups.description: Stay at 45°, never vertical. Forearm on the back, not wrists. Beaten inside: around, never over.

groups.title: Passing under pressure
groups.description: Great passers freeze the defense until the last moment. Step away, step across, step back, step in — pick the one the splitter gives you.

groups.title: Shooting — release and deception
groups.description: Quick beats hard. Ball stays behind the head through the fake. Cross-face near-side every day; the draw shot and the dive progressions once the near-side is automatic.

groups.title: Dryland and conditioning
groups.description: Bands 15 minutes before every water session. Active stretching, never sit-and-hold. Dead Man Swimming when we want a fight.

groups.title: JV starter set
groups.description: The eight clips every JV player should know cold by October. Legs, one release, one defensive stance, one shot.

groups.title: ODP fundamentals — base position and movement
groups.description: USA Water Polo ODP's fundamentals: the base position for passing and shooting (Schroeder/Brooks), and the six movements every session should touch — eggbeater, short breaststroke kicks, spidering, skating, reverse sculling, ball handling.

practices.title: EXAMPLE — Monday after Walnut Hills
practices.intro: **This is a drafted example so you can see the shape; edit or delete it.** Watch the linked clips before practice — 6 minutes total. We are fixing two things from Sunday: hips dropping on perimeter defense, and slow releases when set has position.

blocks.title: Bands + active stretch
blocks.text: On deck before you get wet. Scarecrow rows, internal/external rotation, fake-throws. Nobody in the water without bands.

blocks.title: Legs: eggbeater, stepping, hip swings
blocks.text: Wide knees, still upper body. Stepping drill across the pool in a straight line at the surface. Hip swings — lead foot breaks the surface.

blocks.title: Perimeter defense: shoulder control → foul and deny
blocks.text: Pairs. Hand on the shoulder while he holds it, hands UP when he passes. Then add the foul-and-deny: hit the elbow, back over your hips at 45°, lane hand up. Referees will call the hold if your hips are down — that is the fix from Sunday.

blocks.title: Shooting: cross-face near-side
blocks.text: Shoulders to the cage before the ball arrives. Catch and release, no hesitation. Every rep.

blocks.title: 6-on-5 walk-through
blocks.text: Whiteboard first, then in the water at half speed. Whiteboard GIF goes here once we export one from WPA.

guides.title: Center offense - the Moody keys
guides.subtitle: Heather Moody's keys to the 2 m position, rewritten for St. X centers. Tap any timestamp to jump the player there.
guides.source: For St. X centers. Built 2026-09-10 by the Water Polo build chat from the transcript of "Water Polo: Center Offense Video USAWP Heather Moody" (24:22, YouTube `7QpmV2ELq4Y`, Peter Zamoyski's edit of Heather Moody's talk at the USA Water Polo winter meetings; Moody - Olympic gold 2012). The video's auto-captions are rough ("sinner" = center, "Lake strength" = leg strength); the wording below is a coach's rewrite, not a quote. Timestamps are for the clips worth actually watching.
guides.body:
**Five minutes to read. Then tap the four timestamps marked WATCH - the clips total under four minutes.**

---

## 1. What a good center is made of `0:32`
- **Legs.** You hold a defender up for the whole possession. No legs, no position.
- **Vision.** Know where the ball is the entire time and adjust before it moves, not after.
- **Patience.** Sometimes the ball cannot come in. Hold, wait, then attack the one window you get.
- **Play in the now.** Bad call, offensive foul, turnover - flush it and chase. A center who pouts for two seconds is a center who gives up a counter goal.
- **Controlled intensity.** Know when to be violent and when to be still.
- **Mental toughness.** A tight-called game, or a team that zones all night - you can play a whole game and never touch the ball. That is still your job.

## 2. Your two jobs `2:13`
1. **Gain ball side.** Your perimeter has to get the ball to the side you want to hold. Until then, you are setting up.
2. **Keep ball side.** Once the ball is there, holding it is on you. When the ball comes in: **explode to it.** That move gets the referee's attention (exclusion or foul), gets the separation, or gets the shot. A casual reach gets nothing.

## 3. Where you are `3:33`
Know your spot in front of the cage without looking. Shots go outside the post because the center did not know where he was. **Ideal: on the 3 m line, center cage.** You won't always get it, but that is what you are fighting for.

## 4. The chair - your base position `3:58` **WATCH**
Everything at center starts from here.
- **Sit in a chair.** Knees high, hips directly under you - not in front, not behind.
- **Hip bones to rib cage.** Squish them together. That curves your back the right way and rolls your shoulders forward.
- **Chin on your chest.** This is what stops the offensive foul - you never throw your head back, and when you snap, everything goes forward to the ball.
- **Shoulders out of the water.** Show the referee what the defender is doing to you.
- **Elbows high, level with your shoulders.** It makes you *wide*. A narrow center gets swum around. Wide, you cover your water and can dip and slide to cover more.
- **Hands sculling.**

Why the chair: you can hold this position all possession, and you snap and separate off it at a higher rate because you are over your legs.

## 5. Keep contact - you want his chest `2:52`
Ball-side position is established and kept by **keeping contact with the defender.** You want his chest on your back: you feel where he is about to move or jump and you counter it. If he has separation and only hands on your back, you can't read him.

## 6. The face-to-face start `6:57`
Most teams press. To save your legs, start **face to face**: arm to arm with the defender, **grip at his bicep/tricep**, and **keep space** between you.
- Not tight. Tight puts your hips on already, kills your snap into him, and turns it into a wrestling match.
- With space, when you go, you get momentum into him and he has to back off and reposition.
- **Use your off hand.** Most players turn slowly and lazily and the defender resets in a second. Inside arm goes to work aggressively, then the roadblock goes up (next section).
- You can sit here as long as the ball is on the far side. Conserve energy.

## 7. Turn, spin, seal `9:03` **WATCH**
The technique of the position. **Powerful and explosive** - you are driving into the defender to steal an inch of water and make him backpedal. Do it casually and he repositions or jumps back in front.
- **Turn.** Cage is behind you, ball is on one side. Your **inside arm** (the ball-side arm) goes to the **defender's outside armpit**. Pull him, put your shoulder into that armpit.
- **Spin.** Your shoulder is the navigator. **Put up the roadblock** - your body across his path so he cannot get back in front. Now the order is ball - you - defender. That water in front of you is yours.
- **Seal.** Back into the center spot, into your chair, ball side maintained.
- **Control him from armpit to hip.** Hand on that line; if he moves left, hook a little under the armpit and bring your chair with you, so if the ball comes you can still react.
- **The window is 3-5 seconds** from the ball reaching your side. Be explosive inside it. If it closes - zone, no entry - hold the chair and work on spreading the zone.
- **Anticipate the entry.** Know your passers. When you see it coming, snap to it and you get the separation.

## 8. Getting pushed out `5:38` **WATCH**
Hips down and vertical. If you go horizontal you lose - he pushes you off your spot. When he has your full back to push on, or you're losing contact:
- **Quarter turn.** Wide to narrow - now he only has a shoulder to push against.
- **Explosive breaststroke kick**, dive back in under his armpit, bring him with you.
- **Snap your shoulders square and re-set the chair.** You keep your water.
Don't turn and swim. Quarter turn, kick, dive back.

## 9. Fronted on the counter `12:38` **WATCH**
You come down the pool and the defender is waiting in front.
- **Get to 2 m, a little deep.** Let him take the front.
- **Move him out at 45°.** Never strength on strength straight back - you go nowhere. At 45° he often doesn't feel how far he's going, and now the ball can land where you have inside water. Ball comes to your side: inside arm, outside armpit, turn-spin-seal.
- **If the ball is already deep when you arrive, stop early** and go to work right there.
- **If he over-anticipates the pass** (jumps early): a quick **crossover**, dip back to the 45°, and he's beaten.
- **If he drifts too far from the goal or comes back inside to push:** **spin back toward the cage** to seal him off and keep ball side.
- **If he's quicker than your spin:** match his stroke, then take the hand closest to the ball and spin in. Always the roadblock.

## 10. Drawing the foul `17:08`
- **Hips stay underneath.** Defenders push your hips out of position. Answer with **one quick breaststroke kick** to drive them back - not a steady kick. Rhythm lets him time the jump around you.
- **Absorb the contact.** A lot of it happens underwater and gets no call. Keep your head up so you still know where the ball is.
- **Snap to the ball.** The thing even national teams struggle with. From the chair: drive your **left shoulder into his chest** (arms get a shoulder's length longer), **step with the right leg** (left if you're a lefty), scoop water. It makes the referee look, exposes what he's doing, and opens the shooting lane.
- **Take the chair with you.** Most centers snap without their base and there's nothing behind it. If he over-commits, you have no legs to finish the shot.

## 11. Shooting `18:59`
- **Where the defender is dictates the shot.** Behind you, fronting, on a side - each has its shot.
- **Where you are dictates the shot.** A quarter turn at 5 m is a hard finish. The same thing at 2 m is high percentage.
- **Know the pass.** Some come to your face, some are short, some you catch out of the air. Watch it in, control it - a bad pass doesn't have to be a turnover.

## 12. Against a zone `20:10`
You turn-spin-seal and they drop. Fine - the defense just honored you. Now your job is to **disrupt the zone**: **move across the cage**, not straight back to 2 m. Make the droppers follow you so your perimeter can see how far they really go. If someone crashes, you see it from your chair because you're on your legs - snap away from it and the ball is free.

## 13. Breaking the hold `21:09`
- **Quarter turn** exposes the suit grab to the referee; then dive back to position. If he still has it, spin back to face-to-face for a beat and go again.
- **Low hip grab:** spin away and drop the forearm - it breaks the hold, you separate, then get back.
- **In face-to-face and he's holding:** a quick **barrel roll toward his outside elbow.** He either lets go or it hurts. Don't sit there and hold back.
- **Don't jump and flail at the referee.** You lose your momentum and your position; the call may not come; and you've stopped working with your perimeter.

## 14. Look like the victim `23:04`
Big centers: sit a little lower in the water. Never look like the aggressor even when you are controlling everything.

---

## The card (memorize this)
1. **Chair:** knees high, hips under, chin down, shoulders out, elbows wide, hands sculling.
2. **His chest on your back.** Feel him.
3. **Face to face, arm to arm, with space.** Save your legs.
4. **Ball to your side = 3-5 seconds.** Inside arm to outside armpit. Turn, spin, roadblock, seal.
5. **Pushed out:** quarter turn, one kick, dive back, square up.
6. **Fronted:** 45°, never straight back.
7. **Snap to the ball with your chair.** Left shoulder in, right leg steps.
8. **Bad call? Flush it. Chase.**

*Watch order if you only watch four: 4 → 7 → 8 → 9.*
